https://www.thetimes.com/uk/article/horr.title: Pain, grief, hope: best pictures of 2023 from our photographers
https://www.thetimes.com/uk/article/horr.text:
I cannot even begin to scratch the surface or give a full account of the horrors and grief I have witnessed this year. The latest cycle of violence in the Holy Land is particularly disturbing, as is the seeming loss of focus regarding the conflict in Ukraine.
The one-year anniversary of the full-scale invasion of Ukraine passed in February and there was no significant military breakthrough over the summer. Despite a natural stoicism, there are far too many parents, children and spouses visiting deceased loved one in Ukraine’s expanding cemeteries. A deep sense of grief and shock was omnipresent in Israel as events unfolded following Hamas’ attack at the beginning of October, which in turn, led to retribution against Gaza on an incomprehensible scale.
A personal highlight was the once in a lifetime assignment to Svalbard, the Norwegian archipelago in the high Arctic where we went to report on the geo-political situation in the face of rising global tensions and temperatures.
Despite an uneasy feeling as we are about to enter 2024, it is a privilege to be able to report from the ground as some of the most significant events in our year unfold. We all have our own reasons for doing so and I am one of the naïve ones who hopes it will make a difference.
Thank you for reading, here is a selection of my photographs from 2023.

image.caption: A Ukrainian soldier is treated at a frontline field hospital in the Zaporizhzhya region. He was one of a number of troops injured by an artillery attack on their trench

Another soldier being treated at the same field hospital. Although his injury was severe, with a shrapnel wound to his head, within 15 minutes he was stabilised and moved to a safer clinic further behind the lines

Sometimes it was almost possible to forget that this is a country at war as dancers perform The Snow Queen at the Kyiv Opera House. As a timely reminder, the final scene was interrupted as the air raid alarm sounded and the audience left the building to seek shelter
A priest sanctifies the faithful by sprinkling them and their Easter baskets with holy water on the Orthodox Easter at the Holy Dormition Cathedral in Kyiv

Valentina Zavadsky visited the grave of her grandson Oleksi in Bucha cemetery. He died in combat in Bakhmut 40 days earlier. The 40-day mark is significant in Eastern Orthodox faith as the length of time the soul of the departed remains wandering the earth, coming back to visit their home and their fresh grave.
Members of the Ukrainian territorial defence force line up before heading out to the firing range, just outside the capital, to test out some recently delivered American arms

A yellow wagtail sits atop a sunflower in a field adjacent to Dnipro cemetery. The cemetery has expanded considerably since the start of the war and many were there to pay their respects to departed loved ones

Rishi Sunak, the prime minister, at a “PM connect” event at Topps Tiles in Leicester. He was responding, somewhat theatrically, to a question from the audience as to whether he would be using Topps Tiles in the next Downing street refurbishment

An act of what appeared to be deference by Jeremy Hunt’s treasury team (seeming to bow their heads as they walked past him) as the chancellor prepared for his solo photograph outside number 11 Downing Street before heading to Parliament to deliver his budget

Microphones obscure the eyes of Suella Braverman, then the home secretary, as she addressed the National Conservative Conference in Westminster. She was sacked by the prime minister later in the year following what were generally seen as divisive remarks and questionable language regrading immigrants and pro-Palestinian demonstrations

A juvenile blue tit is caught in a mist net at the Sandwich Bay bird observatory. While ringing data can still be used to study migration and dispersal; today they are primarily used in the study of population change

Israeli troops walk past a car that has bullet holes and blood stains at the site of the Supernova festival near Be’eri, where festival goers were massacred by Hamas as part of the attack on southern Israel on October 7

During the time I was in Israel, journalists were not allowed to enter Gaza. Yet from a hill in Sderot, southern Israel, it was possible to photograph some of the air and artillery strikes on the territory
A crew on top of their tank at a staging post next to Kibbutz Be’eri, one of the Kibbutz close to Gaza that was raided by Hamas, with many residents murdered or kidnapped
During a press conference in Tel Aviv for the families of the hostages taken by Hamas, Osa Me’ir, discovered that the second of her twin siblings had been killed by Hamas

A family from New York take take cover from a rocket attack near Hod Hasharon outside the Israeli capital. Rockets from Gaza reached the city every night through October, most were destroyed by the Iron Dome missile defence system

Close family members grieve the loss of First Lieutenant Amitai Granot during his funeral service at the Mount Herzl cemetery in Jerusalem. He was killed in a clash with Hezbollah in northern Israel the previous day
Israeli Defence Force (IDF) reservists on a house to house clearance training exercise at a model Arab village in Golan

By the end of October, the Ramallah-based health ministry said that more than 100 Palestinians had died in the West Bank since October 7 and there are ongoing weekly protests in Ramallah after prayers on Fridays. A minority show visible support for Hamas, and the protest ends at the Qalandia checkpoint on the edge of town

At the checkpoint, some of the local youth sling stones at Israeli troops, who in turn fire live rounds back, aiming accurately at the legs of each would-be stone thrower caught in the open. The stone-throwing seems to be more bravado than anything else; the Israeli troops appear to be too far away

A woman tows her child while herself being pulled by huskies on the edge of Longyearbyen, the largest town on Svalbard. It is forbidden to leave its limits without a rifle —  unless a companion has one —  in case of attack by polar bear. In theory, people are not allowed to give birth or die on Svalbard. The archipelago is not considered a “life cycle community” and the average stay is three years. In practice, life events sometimes get in the way

Apartments in the Russian coalmining community of Barentsburg, with a bust of Lenin and the words “Communism is our goal”. Until last year there were good relations with Longyearbyen, but after the invasion of Ukraine ties were cut and a majority of the Ukrainian workers left

On route back to the UK from Svalbard we had a stopover in Oslo and took advantage with a visit to the Munch Museum. Other visitors took photographs of each other mimicking the expression of the protagonist in his probably most famous work, The Scream.

A cancelled flight allowed a few hours in Venice before heading to Ukraine. It was packed with tourists taking photographs. I had to wait a while for the crowd to clear before being able to photograph this couple taking a selfie on the Rialto bridge looking down the Grand Canal

During the first of several assignments to Ukraine we met Natalya Verbova at a memorial to her husband and other civilian victims of Russian forces at the State Construction Company in Bucha, the town just outside Kyiv that become synonymous with the brutality of the invaders

https://www.thetimes.com/uk/politics/art.title: The very best pictures of 2023 — and the stories behind them
https://www.thetimes.com/uk/politics/art.text: You might be forgiven for wanting to see the back of 2023, a year that saw bitter conflict reignited in Israel and Gaza, while Russian troops dug in for the long haul in Ukraine. In the UK, the year began with an exhibitionist walrus raising eyebrows in Scarborough, and ended with an apology from Boris Johnson. The general sense of bewilderment, despair and fury was encapsulated in the image of an ancient sycamore felled pointlessly at Hadrian’s Wall. And yet — hope springs: the National Trust reports that green shoots are growing from cuttings taken from that tree. The circle of life was celebrated in full pomp in May as Charles was crowned King. The Lionesses brought us joy then heartache, losing to Spain in the final of the women’s World Cup. Taylor Swift and Elton John entertained us, while the James Webb telescope brought us dazzling images of stars of the cosmic variety. As 2023 comes to an end, we look back with joy, pain and hope on the pictures that defined the year.

image.caption: Three of the stars of Everything Everywhere All at Once pose with their Oscars in the press room at the 95th Academy Awards in Hollywood. The film won seven awards, including best film. From left: Ke Huy Quan (best supporting actor), Michelle Yeoh (best actress) and Jamie Lee Curtis (best supporting actress)

The actor Jared Leto burnishes his party animal credentials at the Met Gala in New York in May. Guests were invited to dress in honour of Karl Lagerfeld; Leto came as the late fashion designer’s cat, Choupette
Lil Nas X makes a sparkling entrance at the Met Gala. The rapper’s outfit consisted of platform boots, a thong, silver body paint — and a reported 5,000 Swarovski crystals

Pope Francis appears to push the boundaries of fashion as he wraps up warm in March. But the image, which went viral, turned out to be AI-generated. A reminder not to believe everything you see online
Elton John fans watch their hero — in the flesh and on the giant screen behind him — as he gives his final UK performance, at Glastonbury on June 25
Writers and actors join forces to picket the Paramount Pictures HQ in Los Angeles on July 14. The strike, over pay and job security, closed down Hollywood for 118 days
The Beckhams keep cool while watching Simon Porte Jacquemus’s fashion show from a boat at the Château de Versailles, near Paris, on June 26
Barbie fans take a group selfie in front of an Oppenheimer poster in Los Angeles. Both films were released on July 21, leading to a cultural phenomenon dubbed “Barbenheimer”
Taylor Swift performs at the Paycor Stadium in Cincinnati, Ohio, in June. The 34-year-old singer is set to earn an estimated $4 billion from her Eras Tour, with 151 shows across five continents
A Banksy mural incorporating a real-life freezer appears in Margate in February. After the freezer went missing twice in a matter of days the artwork was relocated to a local theme park
A giant eyeball displayed on the new Sphere arena in Las Vegas appears to spy on traffic snaking past. The 18,000-seater venue for “immersive” shows opened in September
Surrounded by topless dancers, Madonna, 65, the biggest-selling female artist in history, begins her Celebration tour at the O2 in October in typically raunchy style
The activist Greta Thunberg, 20, is arrested at an oil industry conference in London in October. She was charged with a public order offence and pleaded not guilty. Her trial begins in February

A Leicestershire man’s Ring door camera alerts him to intruders in October. A 50-strong gang in wool overcoats were trespassing in his garden, helping themselves to freshly cut grass. The suspects remain at large
Riot police pass a burnt-out van after mob violence outside a hotel accommodating asylum seekers in the Knowsley area of Merseyside in February. Fifteen people were arrested

The London mayor Sadiq Khan’s chickens come home to roost in November as anti-Ulez protesters flock to south London. Despite a court ruling that expanding the congestion charge zone is lawful, for some it remains a fowl idea

The US president, Joe Biden, meets Rishi Sunak for tea — in special Downing Street mugs — in the No 10 garden during a brief UK visit in July, ahead of a Nato summit in Lithuania to discuss the war in Ukraine
An electoral reform protester covers Keir Starmer in glitter at the Labour Party conference in Liverpool on October 10. Labour were soon selling £20 T-shirts bearing the slogan “Sparkle with Starmer”

Nigel Farage tucks into a “four penis pizza” — from a ram, bull, pig and crocodile — on I’m a Celebrity .. in November. Asked by the host Ant McPartlin if he had “eaten penis” before, Farage replied, “Not regularly”

Boris Johnson faces the Covid inquiry led by Hugo Keith QC on December 6, and admits he and his government were “not as alarmed as we should have been” about the spread of the virus before the first lockdown

The remains of the Crooked House pub near Dudley — which burnt down and was quickly demolished in August after being sold to new owners in July. Police investigating arson have so far arrested six people

Russell Brand leaves the Troubadour theatre in northwest London having performed a comedy routine on September 16 — hours after a Sunday Times investigation revealed that four women had accused him of rape and sexual abuse

The initial arrest of the child-killing nurse Lucy Letby, captured by a police body camera in July 2018. In August this year she received a whole life sentence for murdering seven babies and attempting to murder six more

Amid a police investigation into the Scottish National Party’s finances, Nicola Sturgeon unexpectedly announces her resignation as first minister of Scotland at Bute House on February 15. Sturgeon had served as first minister and SNP leader since 2014

Police carry out a search at the home of Sturgeon and her husband, the former SNP treasurer Peter Murrell, in Glasgow on April 5. Murrell was arrested and questioned, as was Sturgeon herself in June. Both were released without charge and deny any wrongdoing
An orangutan puckers up at Raganun Zoo, Jakarta, Indonesia, in April. Researchers believe the seemingly endearing gesture is actually intended to show dominance and scare off potential predators
An enterprising brown bear snaffles a leaping sockeye salmon making its annual journey upstream at Brooks Falls in the Katmai National Park, Alaska, in August
Bleating sheep and goats replace beeping cars in Madrid in the Trashumancia festival, as shepherds guide their charges through the city following ancient herding routes
A feast for the eyes as a heron in the James River in the US state of Virginia swallows its startled meal whole
A ring of smoke, steam and volcanic gases rises from Mount Etna, Sicily, in August. The gases are emitted at high speed from a single vent in one of Etna’s most active craters
A huge section of cliff collapses overnight onto the beach at Seatown, on the Jurassic Coast in Dorset, in July. Dry weather made the area more prone to rockfalls
An Arctic walrus makes an exhibition of himself in Scarborough in January. It was believed to be the wayfarer nicknamed “Thor”, previously spotted in Hampshire
A good hare day in July in a poppy field near the village of Downton in southern Wiltshire
An intrepid jackdaw perches on a deer to catch flies in Bushy Park, southwest London, in July
A congregation of caimans spills onto the banks of the dried-up Bento Gomes River in the Pantanal wetlands of Brazil. Extensive wildfires ravaged the region in November
Feeling the heat in July, a smarter than average bear takes a dip in a resident’s pool in Burbank, California
England’s Lauren Hemp shoots during the World Cup quarter-final against Colombia in Sydney on August 12. England won 2-1 but lost 1-0 to Spain in the final
Cyclists hurtle through a field of sunflowers on the 124-mile route to Limoges from Libourne for the eighth stage of the Tour de France in July
The Greek artistic swimmer Evangelia Platanioti strikes a pose during her routine at the World Aquatics Championships in Fukuoka, Japan, in July
Cross-country skiers in Ramsau, Austria, negotiate a thin strip of artificial piste in January. Unseasonably warm weather caused problems for ski resorts
The Spanish football federation president, Luis Rubiales, forces an unwanted kiss on the forward Jenni Hermoso after the final. He resigned three weeks later
Novak Djokovic’s championship- winning streak at Wimbledon is ended by Carlos Alcaraz, the 20-year-old Spaniard, in July
Siya Kolisi of South Africa lifts the Rugby World Cup trophy after beating New Zealand 12-11 in the final in Paris on October 28
A shirtless Jack Grealish has an Ibiza moment in June as the Manchester City team celebrate winning the treble
A match at the World Snooker Championship in Sheffield is disrupted as a Just Stop Oil protester covers a table with orange dye on April 17
It’s just stop cricket at Lord’s as a protester interrupts the Ashes Test match in June. He is helped on his way by England’s Jonny Bairstow
Juan Postigo of Spain practises before the first G4D (Golf for the Disabled) Open in Woburn, Bedfordshire, in May
Kevin Sinfield, the England rugby coach, helps his former team-mate Rob Burrow, who has motor neurone disease, finish a marathon in Leeds in May
A Ukrainian soldier covers his ears as he fires a mortar at Russian positions on the front line near Bakhmut, in the Donetsk region, in May
Beachgoers in Odesa are undeterred by signs warning that landmines may be nearby. An estimated two million mines have been left across Ukraine by Russian forces
A display case creates an optical illusion at a café in Avdiivka, in the Donetsk region, as soldiers and locals struggle to maintain a semblance of normal life
Four-year-old Anastasia playfully engages with street art in the city of Bucha, northwest of Kyiv, in January. The work is by the Italian artist TVboy
The Italian poet Dante peers out from a mound of tattered sandbags as Kyiv residents practise yoga in a park behind him in September
Two days after his appointment as foreign secretary, David Cameron meets President Zelensky in November. The former prime minister promised the UK’s continuing support
The Russian fighter jet that caused a US MQ-9 Reaper surveillance drone to crash into the Black Sea in March — after dumping fuel onto it that damaged its propeller
A Ukrainian serviceman lies in a trench during a military exercise near Kharkiv in May. The region, which is close to the Russian border in northeast Ukraine, had been heavily bombarded weeks earlier
An aerial view of the devastation in Bakhmut, taken in June. After five months of bloody combat, the city was captured in May by Russian forces, principally the Wagner group of mercenaries
Standing in a field of corpses in May, the Wagner group leader, Yevgeny Prigozhin, blames Russia’s military leadership for the deaths — lifting the lid on the growing rift with Moscow
Putin accuses Prigozhin of treason on national television in June after the Wagner group’s armed rebellion against the Russian military. Prigozhin called off the mutiny hours later
The Wagner boss is among ten people killed in this plane crash in August. Putin stated it was caused by grenades exploding on board and implied that passengers may have been intoxicated
Torched and abandoned cars at the site of the Supernova music festival in Israel, three miles from Gaza, which was ambushed by Palestinian militants on October 7
Israeli security forces search for personal effects after the Supernova atrocity. The UN has since heard multiple accounts of Hamas soldiers using rape as a weapon of war
In the city of Ashkelon, Israel’s Iron Dome defence intercepts rockets from the Gaza Strip on October 9. The system has largely protected Israel against enemy airstrikes
Bloodstains on a door in Kfar Azar, a kibbutz that was also targeted on October 7. At least 1,200 people were killed in the systemic attacks and 240 hostages were taken to Gaza
Hamas militants drive a kidnapped 85-year-old Israeli citizen and Holocaust survivor, Yaffa Adar, from Kibbutz Nir Oz to Gaza in a golf cart. She was released on November 24
A plume of smoke rises over Gaza in October as Israeli missiles explode. About 16,000 people are estimated to have been killed in the territory since the siege began
In March, months before the recent escalation of the conflict in the Middle East, Palestinians clash with Israeli troops during a raid in Jenin, in the Israeli-occupied West Bank
A distraught woman holds her child close, their bright clothes contrasting with the rubble of Ridwan, a neighbourhood of Gaza, after an Israeli airstrike on October 31
Premature babies are prepared for transport to Egypt after being evacuated from al-Shifa hospital. In November 28 Palestinian infants crossed the border for life-saving treatment

About 20,000 demonstrators, including the families of Israeli hostages held in Gaza, continue a five-day march from Tel Aviv to Jerusalem on November 18. The demonstration aimed to put pressure on the government for the immediate release of captives

After 50 days in captivity, during which she had her ninth birthday, Emily Hand embraces her father, Thomas, after being released on November 25. The Irish-Israeli schoolgirl was at a sleepover on October 7 when she was kidnapped by Hamas

The Israeli prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, left, visits troops in the Gaza Strip on November 26 during the week-long truce when hostages and prisoners were exhanged. Earlier he had vowed to continue the war “until we achieve all our goals”

As the temporary ceasefire between Israel and Hamas begins on November 24, residents of Gaza City emerge from their hiding places and absorb the destruction at ground level. Air strikes and artillery shelling resumed on December 1
An aerial view of the aftermath of a landslide in Alausi, Ecuador, which happened overnight on March 26. Triggered by months of heavy rain, it was half a mile long and killed more than 20 people
Suspected gang members arrive at the Cecot mega-jail in El Salvador in February. It was built by President Nayib Bukele to halt gang violence; human rights groups believe many inmates are innocent
A shellshocked Afghan man stands amid ruins in the Zinda Jan district of the Herat province following an earthquake that flattened entire villages and killed more than 2,000 in October
A fighter jet flies past a high-altitude balloon originating from China that sparked a security alert by entering American airspace. The US air force shot the balloon down on February 4
On the Hawaiian island of Maui, the 200-year-old Waiola Church and nearby Hongwanji Mission are engulfed in flames on August 8. The wildfires killed at least 100 people
Tourists on a beach in Acapulco watch the Mexican navy stage a mock rescue operation in July. Troops have been deployed to protect holidaymakers from local gang violence

Eight people were left dangling over a ravine in Pakistan when a line on their cable car snapped in August. Two were rescued by helicopter, the rest via a makeshift chairlift after a nailbiting 16 hours

A desperate four-day search for the missing Titan submersible ended on June 22 when it was confirmed that the vessel had imploded under intense water pressure near the Titanic wreck, killing all five on board
Members of Albania’s Democratic Party set off smoke bombs and light a small fire in parliament in November in a failed attempt to block the 2024 budget. The flames were quickly extinguished
Migrant families struggle through lily weeds in the Rio Grande Valley in a race to enter the United States from Mexico before asylum rules were tightened in May to clamp down on illegal immigration
A mug shot of Donald Trump after he handed himself in to police in Atlanta in August. He was charged with attempting to subvert the 2020 election before being freed after paying a $200,000 bond

President Joe Biden takes a tumble in June after handing out diplomas at a US air force academy in Colorado. The fall highlighted Biden’s advanced years — though at 81 he is just four years older than Trump

North Korea’s leader, Kim Jong Un, boards his bulletproof train after meeting Vladimir Putin at a Siberian spaceport in September. He is believed to have offered munitions to help  Russia’s war effort in Ukraine

The Wall Street Journal’s Evan Gershkovich waits in a cage for defendants at a Moscow court in October before losing his appeal against espionage charges. If convicted he faces up to 20 years in prison

After floodwater ruined her washing machines, a launderette owner in Pajaro, California, rescues a bagful of coins. The town and surrounding areas were flooded in March when levees failed after violent storms

A pair of 18m-tall rubber ducks undergo sea trials in Hong Kong waters ahead of their starring role in an exhibition by the Dutch installation artist Florantijn Hofman. The show, Double Ducks, opened in June

Mesut Hancer holds the hand of his 15-year-old daughter, Irmak, who died in Kahramanmaras, Turkey, close to the epicentre of a 7.8-magnitude earthquake that struck on February 6. Rescuers braved aftershocks and collapsing buildings as they dug for survivors. The earthquake claimed more than 50,000 lives in Turkey and Syria

King Charles III and Queen Camilla wave to the crowd from the balcony of Buckingham Palace after their coronation on May 6. The service was updated from past ceremonies to represent multiple faiths and cultures
Princess Charlotte and a weary Prince Louis are flanked by their parents at the Westminster Abbey service. The Princess of Wales and her daughter wore crystal headpieces instead of traditional tiaras
The Sword of State is carried through the abbey by Penny Mordaunt, lord president of the council. Onlookers are impressed to see her holding the 3.6kg (8lb) sword firmly aloft for almost an hour

Two-year-old Johann-Maximilian has a nap while waiting patiently for King Charles to arrive in the city of Hamburg on March 31. The trip to Germany was the King and Queen’s first joint state visit abroad

Riders queue for Mr Whippy ice creams in Rockcliffe, Dumfries and Galloway, on a balmy August day. Despite mixed weather, this summer was the UK’s eighth warmest on record, thanks to heatwaves in June and September

The Red Arrows practise manoeuvres after returning to training at RAF Waddington in Lincolnshire on August 11 following a summer break. An inquiry into the aerobatic team uncovered a troubling pattern of harassment against women

A somersault into the sea at Brighton as the sun comes out at last. With disappointing weather through July and August, the mini heatwave in September, which peaked at 33.5C, filled British beaches with revellers

A soldier faints in 29C heat during Trooping the Colour rehearsals on June 10. After a few seconds on the ground he got up and gamely tried to carry on until medics arrived moments later to stretcher him away

Birmingham’s Pride weekend kicked off with a rainbow-themed parade through the city centre in May. The UK’s first Gay Pride rally was in Hyde Park in 1972. This year there were more than 180 Pride events across the country

A fleet of Routemaster buses carries passengers from Warminster to the deserted village of Imber on Salisbury Plain, which opens to the public for only a few days a year — the “Imberbuses” make an annual trip every August

Sir Bobby Charlton (died October 21, aged 86). One of the greatest British footballers, he survived the Munich air crash that killed eight of his Manchester United team-mates in 1958. Alongside his brother Jack he helped England to victory in the 1966 World Cup

Glenda Jackson (died June 15, aged 87). The pioneering actress of stage and screen won numerous awards including two Oscars, for Women in Love and A Touch of Class. No fan of celebrity, she later forged a political career, serving as a Labour MP for 23 years

Tina Turner (died May 24, aged 83). With a string of global hits including What’s Love Got to Do with It in a career spanning five decades, the gravelly voiced singer was a powerhouse hailed as the “Queen of Rock‘n’Roll”

Martin Amis (died May 19, aged 73). A meticulous chronicler of the absurdities of modern life, the influential author of Money and London Fields was named by The Times as one of the 50 greatest British writers since 1945

Sinéad O’Connor (died July 26, aged 56). Celebrated for her beautiful rendition of Nothing Compares 2 U, the Dublin-born singer was a hugely talented artist who attracted controversy  and devotion in equal measure

Burt Bacharach (died February 8, aged 94). A colossus of popular music, the urbane American composer and pianist created complex, evergreen melodies and his songs were recorded by more than a thousand artists

Barry Humphries (died April 22, aged 89). The only guest to appear on Desert Island Discs as two different people, the Australian comedian and writer was best known for his scathing alter ego Dame Edna Everage

Jeff Beck (died January 10, aged 78). Rising to fame as a member of the seminal London band the Yardbirds in the 1960s, Beck was described by Rolling Stone magazine as “one of the most influential lead guitarists in rock”
Raquel Welch (died February 15, aged 82). The actress became a sex symbol and style icon after her role in One Million Years BCand went on to win a Golden Globe in 1973 for The Three Musketeers
Paul O’Grady (died March 28, aged 67). The comedian, actor and broadcaster hit stardom with the drag queen persona Lily Savage, giving up his job as a social worker to promote her talents full time

Henry Kissinger (died November 29, aged 100). A titan of world affairs, the former US secretary of state won a Nobel peace prize yet was accused of war crimes. He said that power was “the ultimate aphrodisiac”
Lord Lawson (died April 3, aged 91). An intellectually bold yet impish chancellor, Nigel Lawson deregulated London’s financial markets before falling out with Margaret Thatcher over Europe
Michael Parkinson (died August 16, aged 88). No celebrity had truly made it until they appeared on the affable Parky’s chat show, which ran for more than 500 episodes from 1971 to 2007

Shane MacGowan  (died November 30, aged 65). Acclaimed for his masterful songwriting, the hard-living frontman of the Celtic punk band the Pogues once observed, “It’s a miracle every morning when you wake up”

George Alagiah (died July 24, aged 67). Born in Sri Lanka, he was a peerless TV presenter, anchoring the News at Six from 2007. Tim Davie, the BBC director-general,  called him one of the “bravest journalists of his generation”

Matthew Perry (died October 28, aged 54). The actor who played the sardonic but loveable Chandler in the hit US sitcom Friends appeared in numerous TV and film roles, but the fame he always craved led to addiction and a life cut short

Benjamin Zephaniah (died December 7, aged 65). A streetwise Rastafarian poet of distinction who overcame a tough childhood in Birmingham, and spells in borstal and prison, to become one of Britain’s best-loved wordsmiths, a novelist, musician and a star of Peaky Blinders

The Rho Ophiuchi cloud complex is the closest star-forming region to Earth, an estimated 390 light years away. Dozens of newly born stars can be seen among thick clouds of cosmic dust. This image from July was captured by the James Webb telescope
An aerial view of Hadrian’s Wall shows the Sycamore Gap tree, which was felled overnight in September. Four people have been arrested for criminal damage but so far no one has been charged

author: The Times and The Sunday Times
